meta.title: CARE HMIS - Open Source Hospital Information System (HIS)
meta.description: CARE HMIS is an open-source, FHIR R5-aligned Hospital Information System (HIS/HMIS) for OPD, IPD, emergency, labs, pharmacy, billing, inventory, reporting, and AI-ready clinical workflows.
meta.ogTitle: CARE HMIS - Open Source Hospital Information System
meta.ogDescription: A modular Hospital Information System connecting patient flow, clinical information, hospital operations, revenue workflows, and AI-ready data.
meta.twitterDescription: Open-source HIS/HMIS for hospitals that need connected OPD, IPD, emergency, lab, pharmacy, billing, reporting, and AI-ready workflows.

hero.title: The open hospital OS for connected care.
hero.body: CARE HMIS is an open-source Hospital Information System that connects patient flow, information flow, and revenue flow across outpatient, emergency, inpatient, labs, pharmacy, billing, and reporting workflows.
hero.videoLabel: CARE HMIS workflow video showing a connected hospital information system
hero.liveWorkflowDetail: Encounters, orders, forms, reports, and operational context.

overview.title: HIS depth with open-source ownership.
overview.body: CARE HMIS is built for hospitals that need more than a digital file. It combines EMR, HMIS, hospital operations, revenue cycle workflows, interoperability, and AI-ready clinical data in one reusable open platform.

clinicalRecord.title: Clinical record
clinicalRecord.text: Patients, encounters, notes, diagnoses, orders, observations, medications, care plans, and discharge summaries.

operations.title: Hospital operations
operations.text: Appointments, queues, beds, wards, departments, staff roles, stock movement, reports, and dashboards.

revenue.title: Revenue cycle
revenue.text: Charge capture, invoices, payments, scheme coverage, claims direction, reconciliation, and accounting integration.

interoperability.title: Interoperability layer
interoperability.text: FHIR-aligned APIs, terminology bindings, ABDM workflows, device integrations, and plugin-based extensions.

problem.title: Software exists. A connected workflow does not.
problem.body: The goal is not electronic records. It is a hospital that can coordinate care, measure quality, manage resources, and safely use assistive AI.

fragments.title: Discrete fragments
fragments.text: Registration, labs, medications, discharge, and billing live as separate events instead of one care story.

disconnected.title: Disconnected workflows
disconnected.text: Orders, results, prescriptions, stock, and dispensing move through silos with no single operational flow.

digitalPaper.title: Digital paper
digitalPaper.text: Forms were digitized without redesigning the work around them, so software becomes one more burden.

lostRevenue.title: Lost revenue
lostRevenue.text: Unbilled services, missed charges, and manual invoicing leave money on the table every day.

flows.title: Records become workflows. Workflows become operations.
flows.body: CARE HMIS treats a hospital as a living system. Every patient event, clinical decision, and financial transaction can move through one connected operating layer.

patient.label: Patient flow
patient.detail: Registration, appointments, OPD, emergency, IPD, ICU, discharge, and follow-up.

information.label: Information flow
information.detail: Encounters, orders, results, records, decisions, and longitudinal clinical context.

revenue.label: Revenue flow
revenue.detail: Charges, invoices, scheme coverage, payments, and reconciliation as care is delivered.

encounters.title: One platform for every care setting.
encounters.body: CARE supports the full patient journey, while keeping clinical documentation consistent across hospitals, clinics, homes, and virtual visits.
encounters.videoLabel: CARE HMIS questionnaire and doctor notes workflow

outpatient.title: Outpatient
outpatient.text: Clinical visits linked to the patient record.

inpatient.title: Inpatient
inpatient.text: Admissions, rounds, orders, notes, and discharge.

coreModules.title: The workflows a hospital expects, built on one core.
coreModules.body: Modules are not isolated applications. They share patients, encounters, orders, observations, roles, reports, and audit trails.

clinicalData.title: Clinical data capture
clinicalData.text: Structured forms, symptoms, conditions, orders, medication requests, and observations.

scheduling.title: Scheduling
scheduling.text: Appointment calendars, public facility pages, doctor availability, and open slots.

queues.title: Queues
queues.text: Doctor, department, pharmacy, billing, and custom service queues for high-volume settings.

formBuilder.title: EMR form builder
formBuilder.text: Configurable department forms mapped to interoperable clinical resources.

beds.title: Bed management
beds.text: Live locations, beds, admission status, hierarchy, and availability.

hierarchy.title: Administrative hierarchy
hierarchy.text: Facility, district, state, program, and national structures with data segregation.

rbac.title: RBAC and audit
rbac.text: Granular role-based access control for doctors, nurses, admins, and health workers.

reports.title: Dynamic reports
reports.text: Treatment summaries, discharge summaries, dashboards, and custom operational reports.

workflows.title: See the hospital OS as real product workflows.
workflows.body: These are not static module names. CARE HMIS supports live workflows across bed management, clinical drawings, and dynamic reporting on the same shared patient and facility data layer.

beds.title: Bed management
beds.text: Track beds, locations, admissions, discharge states, and live availability across hospital hierarchies.

drawings.title: Clinical drawings
drawings.text: Capture drawings, body maps, annotations, and visual clinical context directly in the patient record.

reports.title: Dynamic reports
reports.text: Generate operational and clinical reports from shared encounters, forms, orders, and care activity.

departments.title: One operating layer across hospital departments.
departments.body: CARE HMIS gives hospitals a shared information system for clinical, administrative, operational, and financial work. Each department can keep its workflow while contributing to one longitudinal record.

frontDesk.title: Front desk
frontDesk.text: Registration, demographics, patient search, appointments, queues, and visit creation.

opd.title: OPD and clinics
opd.text: Consultations, notes, prescriptions, investigations, follow-up, referrals, and summaries.

emergency.title: Emergency
emergency.text: Rapid registration, triage direction, emergency encounters, orders, observation, and handover.

inpatient.title: Inpatient wards
inpatient.text: Admissions, bed allocation, rounds, nursing updates, orders, discharge, and transfers.

icu.title: ICU and critical care
icu.text: TeleICU extension, vitals/device direction, remote review, video, and escalation workflows.

laboratory.title: Laboratory
laboratory.text: Lab orders, specimen tracking direction, results, diagnostic reports, and LOINC/UCUM alignment.

pharmacy.title: Pharmacy
pharmacy.text: Prescriptions, dispensing, substitutions, stock alerts, procurement, inventory, and audit trails.

billing.title: Billing and accounts
billing.text: Service charges, invoices, payments, insurance/scheme support, and reconciliation workflows.

administration.title: Administration
administration.text: Facilities, departments, users, roles, access control, audit logs, reports, and operational analytics.

operations.title: The back office is clinical infrastructure.
operations.body: Labs, pharmacy, stock, billing, and accounting are not downstream admin tasks. They are part of the same clinical timeline.

lab.title: Lab and diagnostics / LMIS
lab.text: Clinicians order tests, labs track samples, results attach to the record, and observations use standard codes and units.

pharmacy.title: Pharmacy and inventory
pharmacy.text: Prescriptions flow into dispensing, substitutions, stock movement, alerts, procurement, and supply chain workflows.

billing.title: Billing and accounting
billing.text: Cash, insurance, government schemes, invoices, payment capture, and reconciliation connect back to care activity.

standards.title: Built for exchange, analytics, and assistive AI.
standards.body: CARE HMIS is standards-first, API-first, modular, cloud agnostic, mobile-first, and designed to be extended without forking the core.

apps.title: Extend the hospital OS without breaking the core.
apps.body: CARE Apps add national rails, TeleICU, AI documentation, devices, claims, token display, messaging, and analytics through a plugin layer. AI drafts. Humans decide. CARE records.

abdm.title: ABDM
abdm.text: M1, M2, M3 and identity workflows through plugins.

teleicu.title: TeleICU
teleicu.text: Camera, vitals, remote review, and critical care extension.

scribe.title: Care Scribe
scribe.text: Multilingual voice fill and assistive documentation.

tokenDisplay.title: Token display
tokenDisplay.text: Queue and token screens for TVs and public counters.

labsDevices.title: Labs and devices
labsDevices.text: Orders, results, PACS, and bedside integrations.

claimsMessaging.title: Claims and messaging
claimsMessaging.text: HCX, reminders, analytics, and patient communication.

apps.responsibleAiBody: Voice fill, document understanding, record summaries, discharge drafts, and decision support sit on top of structured clinical data with human review.

implementation.title: A serious HIS rollout is product, process, and governance.
implementation.body: CARE HMIS deployments can start with a focused hospital workflow and expand into a complete Hospital Information System. The same open core supports phased adoption, local configuration, partner-led implementation, and long-term release upgrades.

masterData.title: Master data
masterData.text: Facilities, departments, rooms, beds, services, staff, user roles, tariffs, and drug catalogues.

workflowMapping.title: Workflow mapping
workflowMapping.text: OPD, emergency, IPD, pharmacy, lab, billing, and discharge flows aligned to local practice.

formsTerminology.title: Forms and terminology
formsTerminology.text: Configurable EMR forms, FHIR resources, ValueSets, SNOMED CT, LOINC, UCUM, and ICD-10.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.text: ABDM, devices, lab systems, accounting tools, messaging, analytics, payments, and partner plugins.

security.title: Security model
security.text: Role-based access, audit trails, hosting choices, data ownership, backup, and operational controls.

adoption.title: Adoption plan
adoption.text: Training, phased rollout, support desk, reporting cadence, feedback loops, and release upgrades.

deployment.title: CARE HMIS {version} is live across multiple deployments.

what.question: What is CARE HMIS?
what.answer: CARE HMIS is an open-source Hospital Information System and Hospital Management Information System built around CARE Core. It connects clinical records, hospital operations, billing, reporting, integrations, and AI-ready workflows on one standards-based platform.

emrOrHis.question: Is CARE HMIS an EMR or a full HIS?
emrOrHis.answer: CARE HMIS includes EMR capabilities, but it is broader than an electronic medical record. It supports patient registration, OPD, emergency, inpatient care, labs, pharmacy, inventory, billing, reporting, access control, integrations, and deployment workflows.

selfHosted.question: Can CARE HMIS be self-hosted?
selfHosted.answer: Yes. CARE is designed for self-hosted, cloud, hybrid, and on-premise deployment models, so hospitals and governments can own their infrastructure and avoid software licence lock-in.

departments.question: Which hospital departments can CARE HMIS support?
departments.answer: CARE HMIS can support front desk, OPD, emergency, inpatient wards, ICU and TeleICU workflows, laboratory, pharmacy, inventory, billing, administration, analytics, and patient-facing workflows.

interoperability.question: How does CARE HMIS support interoperability?
interoperability.answer: CARE HMIS is standards-first, with FHIR R5-aligned resources, open APIs, terminology support for SNOMED CT, LOINC, UCUM and ICD-10, and plugin-based integrations for national rails, devices, labs, claims, messaging, and analytics.

ai.question: How is AI used in CARE HMIS?
ai.answer: AI is assistive and human-in-the-loop. CARE HMIS can support voice fill, documentation drafts, document understanding, summaries, and decision-support workflows on top of structured clinical data and audit-aware processes.

final.title: Intelligent hospitals need connected workflows first.
final.body: CARE HMIS gives hospitals the shared operating layer for clinical work, operations, revenue, analytics, and carefully governed AI.
